title: Chromatic number: subset DP over independent sets vs inclusion-exclusion
problem_statement: Given a simple undirected graph G on vertices 0..n-1, compute its chromatic number chi(G): the least k such that the vertices can be coloured with k colours so that adjacent vertices get different colours (chi = 0 for the empty graph on 0 vertices).

input.size_measure: n vertices and up to n(n-1)/2 edges, given as an edge list. Vertex subsets are n-bit masks (n <= 18 in the harness), and operations on them count as unit cost.

algorithms.name: subset DP over all independent sets
algorithms.idea: chi(S) = 1 + min chi(S \ T) over the non-empty independent sets T contained in S, computed for every vertex subset S in increasing order. T ranges over all independent subsets, not only the maximal ones.
algorithms.pseudocode: independent[S] for all S (one vertex at a time); chi[0] = 0; for S = 1 .. 2^n - 1: chi[S] = min over submasks T != 0 of S with independent[T] of chi[S ^ T] + 1
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(3^n) on every input: exactly 3^n - 2^n inner iterations (one per pair T, S with T a non-empty subset of S), plus Theta(2^n) to tabulate the independent subsets
algorithms.correctness: An optimal colouring's colour classes are independent; removing one class T leaves a (chi(S) - 1)-colouring of S \ T, and conversely adding the class T to a colouring of S \ T colours S. Induction over |S|. This is the subset dynamic programme that Bjorklund, Husfeldt & Koivisto (2009, section 1.3) describe as going back at least to Lawler 1976, whose running time they bound within a polynomial factor of 3^n. Lawler restricts T to maximal independent sets of G[S], which gives O((1 + 3^(1/3))^n) = O(2.4423^n); that refinement is not implemented here.

algorithms.name: inclusion-exclusion (Bjorklund-Husfeldt-Koivisto)
algorithms.idea: Let a(S) = number of non-empty independent sets inside S. Then c_k = sum_S (-1)^(n-|S|) a(S)^k counts the k-tuples of independent sets that cover V, and chi(G) is the least k with c_k > 0. Tabulate a(S) for all S with a(S) = a(S - v) + a(S - N[v]) + 1, then try k = 1, 2, ... keeping a(S)^k by one multiplication per subset per round.
algorithms.time_complexity: (2 chi(G) + 2) 2^n arithmetic operations: one pass of two additions per subset to tabulate a, then chi(G) rounds of one multiplication and one addition per subset. The integers have at most n chi(G) bits. That is O(n 2^n) arithmetic operations in the unit-cost model (chi(G) <= n), Theta(n 2^n) whenever chi(G) = Theta(n), and O(n^4 2^n) bit operations with schoolbook multiplication
algorithms.correctness: Bjorklund, Husfeldt & Koivisto 2009: by inclusion-exclusion, sum over X of (-1)^|X| a'(X)^k, with a'(X) the number of sets from the family disjoint from X, counts the k-tuples covering V (their formula (1.1), written here with S = V \ X). Their Lemma 7: chi(G) <= k iff the number of covers by k non-empty independent sets is positive, since a cover gives a colouring by giving each vertex the first set containing it. The recurrence for a(S) splits the independent sets into those avoiding v and those containing v (equation (4.1) of the paper, in complemented form).

relationship: Theta(3^n) -> O(n 2^n) (unit-cost arithmetic): one exponential base replaced by a smaller one, still exponential. Restricting the DP to maximal independent sets gives O(2.4423^n) (Lawler 1976). Further refinements of that line are listed in Table 1.2 of Bjorklund, Husfeldt & Koivisto, e.g. Eppstein 2003. Inclusion-exclusion reaches 2^n n^(O(1)). Deciding chi(G) <= k is NP-complete (Karp 1972), so a polynomial-time algorithm would imply P = NP; hence primary T6 with secondary T8.

sources.title: A note on the complexity of the chromatic number problem
sources.note: Subset DP restricted to maximal independent sets. The bound O(2.4423^n) = O((1 + 3^(1/3))^n) is quoted here from Table 1.2 of Bjorklund, Husfeldt & Koivisto and from the abstract and introduction of Eppstein 2003; the paper itself was not read for this entry.

sources.authors: Bjorklund, A.; Husfeldt, T.; Koivisto, M.
sources.title: Set partitioning via inclusion-exclusion
sources.note: Read in the authors' open-access version (url). The abstract gives 2^n n^O(1) time for Chromatic Number. Proposition 1 states that deciding chi(G) <= k takes O(2^n n k polylog(nk)) time and O(2^n n) space, raising each a(X) to the k-th power with log k multiplications of nk-bit numbers. The implementation here instead tries k = 1, 2, ... with one multiplication per subset per round.

verification.method: V1: both implementations agree with each other and with an independent oracle (exact backtracking k-colouring search in harness.py, which checks that chi colours suffice and chi - 1 do not) on G(n, p) graphs with p = 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, empty and complete graphs, cycles, random bipartite graphs and disjoint triangles, n = 0..14 (6 instances per n). V2 on G(n, 0.8) random graphs: runtimes fitted against 3^n (subset DP, n = 7..13) and n 2^n (inclusion-exclusion, n = 10..18). experiments/2026-10-07_chromatic_probe.py confirms the DP's exact inner-iteration count 3^n - 2^n for n = 6..12, and prints chi of each timing instance: chi/n between 0.50 and 0.71 for n = 6..18, so the number of inclusion-exclusion rounds grows linearly over the measured range. That is a measured property of these instances for n <= 18, not an asymptotic claim about G(n, 0.8). The fit cannot resolve the factor n: in the probe the same inclusion-exclusion timings gave alpha = 0.954 against n 2^n and 1.069 against 2^n (both inside the tolerance), and 0.674 against 3^n (rejected).

caveats: The O(n 2^n) count is for unit-cost arithmetic. The numbers a(S)^k have up to n chi(G) bits (at most 180 bits at n = 18 here), so the bit complexity carries extra polynomial factors. Bjorklund, Husfeldt & Koivisto also give a polynomial-space variant running in O(2.2461^n) time (their Proposition 7). The inclusion-exclusion algorithm's running time depends on chi(G) through the number of rounds. The subset DP's does not. Both need Theta(2^n) memory. The 3^n bound is for the plain DP over all independent subsets as implemented, not for Lawler's published algorithm, which enumerates only maximal independent sets.
notes: Inclusion-exclusion counts covers rather than searching for colourings, which is why it can afford to look at each subset only once per round. The same framework also counts proper k-colourings, i.e. computes the chromatic polynomial, through counting partitions into independent sets (BHK Proposition 2, via their Theorem 2). Compare pairs/permanent-naive-vs-ryser, another inclusion-exclusion algorithm, and pairs/tsp-brute-vs-held-karp (subset DP).
